recognize_zh: 視野中央一顆紅血球內有數顆粗大、深藍紫色的點狀包涵體，符合標題所示的粗嗜鹼性點彩（coarse basophilic stippling）；但這些顆粒集中在細胞下緣而非均勻散布，型態上也需與 Pappenheimer 小體鑑別。
features: Central red cell containing several coarse, dark blue-purple punctate granules
Granules clustered toward one margin of the cell rather than evenly dispersed
Occasional other red cells with faint fine stippling
Background mild anisopoikilocytosis with some elongated, folded and stomatocyte-like cells
No nucleated red cells, leukocytes or parasites in the field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows mild anisopoikilocytosis with scattered folded and stomatocyte-like red cells. A central erythrocyte contains several coarse, dark blue-purple granules; they are clustered along one margin rather than distributed evenly throughout the cell, and only faint fine stippling is seen in occasional other cells. The findings are compatible with coarse basophilic stippling as labeled (as seen in lead poisoning), but the peripheral clustering also raises Pappenheimer bodies, which a Prussian blue stain would distinguish. Correlation with blood lead and zinc protoporphyrin levels is recommended.

ddx.vs: Pappenheimer bodies are a few peripheral clustered granules that stain with Prussian blue, whereas basophilic stippling is iron-negative ribosomal RNA dispersed throughout the cell.
A Howell-Jolly body is usually a single, larger, round, dense DNA remnant rather than multiple small granules.
Parasites have a ring of cytoplasm with a chromatin dot and may show pigment or tetrads, unlike simple punctate granules.
An overlying platelet has a granular center with a pale cytoplasmic halo and lies in a different focal plane.
